title: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life

concepts.learning_objective: Explain when and on what basis handpicking is used to separate a solid mixture.
Describe threshing as beating stalks to separate grains and place it in the sequence of grain processing.
Explain how wind or blown air separates heavier and lighter components of a mixture.
State that threshers carry out threshing and winnowing together.
Explain that sieving separates solids whose particles differ in size.
Relate the size of the holes of a sieve to which particles pass through and which remain.
Explain how evaporation separates a solid dissolved in a liquid.
Describe how common salt is obtained from seawater using sunlight and air.
Define sedimentation as the settling of a heavier insoluble component in a liquid.
Explain decantation and its everyday uses and limits.
Explain how filtration separates insoluble solids from a liquid and name the residue and filtrate.
Choose a suitable filter based on the size of its pores and of the particles to be removed.
Explain how churning separates butter from curd or cream from milk.
Use the magnetic nature of substances such as iron to separate them from a mixture.
Distinguish separating two useful components from removing an unwanted one.
Match a mixture to a suitable method of separation.
Plan a sequence of methods to separate a mixture of more than two components.
